page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 64 virtual CPUs (32 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom-tier results in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, supported by strong memory bandwidth for large block read-only operations (189.99 GB/sec) and high scores in Passmark CPU extended instructions. Large-scale multi-threaded tasks, database operations, and static web serving throughput consistently perform in the middle tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m5d.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring high-capacity local NVMe storage alongside substantial memory and compute resources. The inclusion of local NVMe SSDs eliminates the need for external block storage for temporary data, optimizing resource-per-cost ratios. This profile is highly suitable for databases, multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from high-speed local scratch space.
